ballotQuestions.statewideIntro: Five proposed amendments to the City Charter. Every voter in the five boroughs gets the same five questions, each a separate yes or no.
ballotQuestions.source: Commission on Government Efficiency, the 2026 New York City Charter Revision Commission. Appendix A, Proposed Questions, adopted at the final public meeting on July 23, 2026.

items.title: Speed Up Process for Granting a Revocable Consent to Use Public Space
items.summary: Simplify process to use public space for uses such as ramps, planters and cafes, by removing mandatory hearings and Council disapproval of sidewalk cafes, while maintaining community and Council input.
items.yes: speeds up process to use public space while maintaining community input.
items.no: maintains longer process with mandatory public hearing to use public space and Council review of sidewalk cafes.

items.title: Reduce City Contractor Paperwork; Require Regular Meetings of Procurement Policy Board
items.summary: Reduce paperwork for City contractors by authorizing Procurement Policy Board to simplify contractor questionnaire. Require quarterly meetings of the Procurement Policy Board. Remove mandatory hearing for required client services report.
items.yes: amends Procurement Policy Board authority, including to simplify contractor questionnaire; authorizes Mayor to delegate certain contract approvals.
items.no: leaves laws unchanged, with Mayor and Comptroller maintaining longer questionnaire.

items.title: Speed Up Street Safety Projects, Disposition of Unused City Property, Office Leasing
items.summary: Simplify review of street safety projects to reduce construction timelines. Fast track disposition of unused City property with approval from City Planning Commission. Expedite leasing offices used for City workforce.
items.yes: simplifies street project approval, City property disposition and office leasing.
items.no: maintains intra-agency consultation for road projects, Council approval for City property dispositions and Council disapproval of office leases.

items.title: Simplify Building Permitting and Move Waterfront Permitting to Department of Buildings
items.summary: Create centralized construction permits hub to simplify permitting. Move waterfront permitting from Department of Small Business Services to Department of Buildings. Allow construction approval by additional Department of Buildings officials.
items.yes: simplifies permitting by authorizing a centralized permitting hub, moving waterfront permitting to Department of Buildings, and allowing additional Department of Buildings officials to issue approvals.

items.title: Set Contribution Targets for Rainy Day Fund to Promote Sufficient Budgetary Reserves
items.summary: Set target amount of money to hold in reserve funds, including rainy day fund, to address unexpected financial hardships in future years, and require development of methodology to calculate contributions.
items.yes: requires Mayor to develop methodology for calculating deposits to rainy day fund, with deposits subject to approval in the City budget.
items.no: leaves laws unchanged, with no reserves target.

register.heading: Register to vote
register.deadline: Your registration has to be received by a board of elections by Saturday, October 24. New York has no same-day registration, so October 24 is the last day for online, mail and in person. Moving? The deadline to update your address is October 19. You can register if you are a U.S. citizen, 18 by Election Day, and have lived at your address for 30 days by Election Day. Registering is free.

blocks.label: Online
blocks.text: The fastest way. Register or update your address at e-register.vote.nyc. You will need the ID number from a New York State driver license, learner permit, or non-driver ID. No DMV ID? Use the State portal at elections.ny.gov, or the paper form below.

blocks.label: By mail
blocks.text: Print the form, fill it out, sign it by hand, and mail it to Board of Elections, 32 Broadway, 7th Floor, New York, NY 10004-1609. It has to arrive by October 24, so mail it early. To have a form mailed to you, call 1-866-VOTE-NYC.

blocks.label: In person
blocks.text: Any borough Board of Elections office, any DMV office, or a State agency registration site, by October 24. In Brooklyn: 345 Adams Street, 4th Floor, Brooklyn, NY 11201, 1-718-797-8800.

blocks.label: Not sure?
blocks.text: Check whether you are registered, and at which address, at amiregistered.vote.nyc. If you registered recently and no card arrives within four to six weeks, call 1-866-VOTE-NYC.

items.text: Voter registration deadline. Your application has to be received by a board of elections by this date to vote in the general election. How to register.
Last day to apply online or by mail for an early mail or absentee ballot.

Early voting. Nine days. Mostly 9 AM to 5 PM; Oct 27 and 28 run 10 AM to 8 PM, Oct 29 runs 8 AM to 4 PM. Your early voting site is usually not your Election Day site, so check both above. You can also drop off a completed mail ballot at any early voting site in your county during this window.
Last day to apply in person at your county board of elections for an early mail or absentee ballot.
Election Day. Polls open 6 AM to 9 PM. If you are on line at 9 PM you get to vote.
Last day to postmark a mail ballot. You can also drop it at any poll site by 9 PM, or at your borough board of elections office by 9 PM.
Last day a postmarked mail ballot can arrive at your county board of elections and still be counted.

earlyVoting.heading: The nine days of early voting
earlyVoting.intro: Hours below are the ones the NYC Board of Elections has posted for the general election. Most days are 9 AM to 5 PM, with two evening days (Tuesday and Wednesday, until 8 PM) and one early day (Thursday, opens at 8 AM). Any early voting site in your county works, but the one assigned to you above is the one the Board expects you at.

notes.heading: Two things worth knowing
notes.text: Two things worth knowing. Poll sites move. The Board of Elections mails a notice before every election, and the assignment shown here is the one the Board has on file right now, so check back in late October before you go. Candidates shown are from the State Board of Elections certification of September 3, 2026. Civil Court judges are certified separately by the City Board of Elections and are added here when that list is posted.

ifSomethingIsWrong.heading: If something is wrong
ifSomethingIsWrong.text: Call 1-866-VOTE-NYC (1-866-868-3692). The Brooklyn office of the Board of Elections is at 345 Adams Street, 4th Floor, Brooklyn, NY 11201, 1-718-797-8800. You can check your registration and request a mail ballot at vote.nyc. If you are told you cannot vote, ask for an affidavit ballot. They have to give you one.
